tldr: This letter-scale note presents a continuum-certified stipulated benchmark separation for optional-priority allocation. The literal note-defined lexicographic estimate-then-optimize benchmark has Gaussian maximum scaled causal regret \(V_{\mathrm{PI}}>0.195163624646\), while a fully specified portable rational rule satisfies \(V_*=V\le\sup_{h\in H}R(h,d_c)<0.154778948570\), giving \(V_{\mathrm{PI}}-V_*>0.040384676076\). The unchanged directed certificate covers all 484 observation cells and the continuous effect square. At the same witness effect, positive original-trial support, conditional variance and score variance are proved for every \(n\ge16\). The retained original-record theorem proves \(M_n\to V_*\) with total data-only budget-feasible attainment, and both fixed rules have uniform risk transfer. The contribution is incremental and below-field. The literal selector is not attributed to any published paper or workflow, and \(d_c\) is a feasible improving rule whose optimality, finite-sample superiority and pointwise dominance are not proved. Sunada--Izumi Example 3.8 already establishes the closest qualitative plug-in-suboptimality phenomenon; this note contributes only the certified specialization to its distinct optional-priority game.
